clue.text: Very funny chair — style is extraordinary

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the ordinary, so the letters of the two words are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A chair of some outlandish design is said to be hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is extraordinary' rearranges the ten letters of CHAIR and STYLE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysterical in its informal sense describes something so comic it makes people laugh uncontrollably.

clue.text: Horse needing a supplementary bridle

parts.note: a hack is a horse for ordinary riding
more means additional, extra

explanation.surface: A horse needs an extra bridle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' looks like the definition, but it gives HACK; the answer is the bridle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackamore is a kind of bitless bridle that works by pressure on the horse's nose.

clue.text: Stranger in street becomes most noticeable — Arts able

clue.text: Indication of immoral area? Don't go through it!

definitions.meaning: a red lamp in the window traditionally marked a brothel, hence a district of vice
the traffic signal that tells drivers to stop

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: the lamp signalling a brothel, and the traffic signal ordering a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A red lamp marks a brothel district, and a red traffic signal forbids passing.

clue.text: Cornish twerp getting animated about the lady architect

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the pronoun, signalling a container
animated means set in lively motion, so the letters of the two words are stirred into a new order

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A small Cornish idiot becomes lively around a female designer of buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting animated' shuffles the Cornish twerp's twelve letters and 'about' wraps them round the lady; the architect is the one who rebuilt London's churches.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral in London and many City churches after the Great Fire.

clue.text: Workers scowl when a boss initially intrudes

indicators.note: the pieces push their way into the scowl word, so one sits inside another

parts.note: to lour (or lower) is to frown or scowl

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: Staff frown when the manager pushes in.
explanation.walkthrough: LOUR is an old word for frown; A and B (the first letter of 'boss') go into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is a collective word for workers, the workforce as a body.

clue.text: English school backs providing information

indicators.note: backs here means goes into reverse, so the joined pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A school in England provides supporters with the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not a place of learning but a group of whales, POD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for inside information or the lowdown on something.

clue.text: Boy upset about 'is girl giving the brush-off

indicators.note: the turned word goes around the other pieces, signalling a container
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a dropped-aitch way of writing his, taken as the letters shown
miss is a young woman

explanation.surface: A boy is distressed that his girlfriend has dumped him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reads the boy backwards (DAL), and 'about' wraps that round the dropped-aitch his and the girl; the surface hides a jilted boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissal is a rejection or sending away, just as a brush-off is a curt rebuff.

clue.text: Spicy berries — horse gobbles 'em up

indicators.note: the horse swallows the other piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: a pinto is a piebald horse

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a short form of them, taken as the letters shown

explanation.surface: A horse wolfs down some hot berries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads 'em backwards in this down clue and 'gobbles' puts it inside the horse; pimento berries are allspice, not the red pepper of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimento is another name for allspice, the dried berries of a West Indian tree.

clue.text: Press here to announce schedule of events

indicators.note: announcing is saying out loud, so the word is the one that sounds the same

parts.note: a calendar lists events by date

explanation.surface: An instruction to push a button here to read out the programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like a command in the surface but is a noun, a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A calender is a machine of heated rollers that presses cloth or paper to smooth it.

clue.text: Thus the maiden for the lad to embrace?

definitions.text: Thus the maiden for the lad to embrace?

indicators.note: the boy goes round the other pieces, so they sit inside him

parts.note: a boy is a lad
so means thus, in this way
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A buxom young woman whom a lad would like to hug.
explanation.walkthrough: BOY embraces SO and M; read whole, the clue describes a full-figured girl a boy wants to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosomy means having a large bust, a fitting picture of a maiden the lad wants to hug.

clue.text: A qualified educationist may be lying

parts.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education, a teaching degree

explanation.surface: A trained teacher could be telling untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' looks like telling lies, but means lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Abed means in bed, so someone abed is lying down resting.

clue.text: Untroubled at home by wrongful US action

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: something wrongful is not right, so the letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone at home is unbothered by an unjust American move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongful' rearranges USACTION to SOUCIANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insouciant means carefree and unconcerned, without worry.

clue.text: Where farrier works without any great preparation

definitions.meaning: a farrier shoes horses, working on their feet
an idiom for doing something improvised, while moving

explanation.walkthrough: A farrier works on a horse's foot; the same phrase means doing things on the spur of the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means literally on a horse's foot, and figuratively doing things impromptu, without planning.

clue.text: Put up with girl, a scrubber

parts.note: to house someone is to put them up, give lodging
a maid is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone offers lodging to a girl who scrubs floors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrubber' is British slang for a promiscuous woman, but here it is literal: one who scrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A housemaid is a female servant doing cleaning, someone who scrubs floors.

clue.text: First female MP: a short account

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a story is an account

explanation.surface: A quick report on the earliest woman in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of STORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy Astor was the first woman to take her seat in the House of Commons, in 1919.

clue.text: Hardy boy I brought up with external minute, support

clue.text: Weird creepiness is not wanted in demeanour

indicators.note: weird means strange, so the letters are reshuffled
the letters of is are not wanted, so they are left out of the mixed pool

explanation.surface: Strange creepy behaviour is not welcome in someone's manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not wanted' takes I and S out of CREEPINESS; 'Weird' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence is a person's bearing or air, the impression of their manner.

clue.text: Each sheep is to show good appetite

parts.note: a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: Every sheep is expected to eat heartily.
explanation.walkthrough: TUP is a dialect word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat up is to finish a meal with relish, a sign of hearty appetite.

clue.text: Insult a priest in type

indicators.note: the priest sits inside the type word, a container

parts.note: a font is a set of type
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: Someone slights a clergyman in print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the priest's title inside the type: 'type' means printing type here, not a kind or sort.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is an open insult or slight.

clue.text: Provider of beef tea sailor's drunk

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: drunk means reeling, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A seaman's tea, laced with drink, comes from a cattle farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' jumbles the sailor's letters to ROLAIS; 'beef tea' looks like a single drink, but the beef belongs to the definition and the tea is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charolais is a French breed of cattle raised for beef.

clue.text: Fix artist up with stove

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a range is a kitchen stove

explanation.surface: Someone mends a painter's oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RA to AR.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange is to fix or settle, as in arranging a date.

clue.text: Fool I left imprisoned in semi-darkness

indicators.note: the pieces are locked inside the fool word, a container

parts.note: a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot jailed me and left me in the gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned' puts I and L inside TWIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit means lit by twilight, dimly lit between day and night.

clue.text: Pudding will be taken around hospital room later

indicators.note: the pudding word goes around the other piece, a container

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert
a ward is a room in a hospital

explanation.surface: Dessert will be served round the hospital ward later.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British slang for pudding, the sweet course.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterwards means at a later time, subsequently.

clue.text: Heading off in the country to find river

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, is taken off

parts.note: rural means in the country

explanation.surface: Someone leaves town to find a stream in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' removes the first letter of RURAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural is a river flowing from the Ural Mountains to the Caspian Sea.

clue.text: Extra number going to the dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An additional person makes up numbers at the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a no-ball is an illegal delivery, one of the extras scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-ball is one of the extras in cricket, runs added to the score not off the bat.

clue.text: Having cut charge to much less than a pound, give up

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: rent is a charge for a property
an ounce is one-sixteenth of a pound weight

explanation.surface: Someone cuts their rent to almost nothing and quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money, but it is a weight: an OUNCE is far less. 'Having cut' drops the T of RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce is to give up a claim or right formally.

clue.text: Poker cuts academic work short

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: study is academic work

explanation.surface: Card playing interrupts study.
explanation.walkthrough: Stud is a form of poker in which some cards are dealt face up.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud is a variety of poker, played with some cards dealt face up.

clue.text: New recruits offer payment before start of training

parts.note: to tender is to offer
a fee is a payment

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Fresh recruits are offered pay before training begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes the T from 'training'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderfeet are newcomers or novices, especially new Scouts or settlers.
